title: Staged experiments + rollback guidance for SDK & API: function-calling, structured output, streaming
creator: Morgan Reyes
description:
Objective: safely roll out the new SDK + API surface for function-calling, structured output, and streaming with an emphasis on staged experiments, clear rollback triggers, and consumer migration guidance. This ticket captures the go/no-go criteria for each stage, telemetry knobs, signoff owners, and the runbook pages that support quick remediation.

Scope:
- API surface: function-calling schema, structured-output hints, streaming chunked responses.
- SDKs: Node, Python, and Go client updates that add opt-in experiment flags and compatibility shims.
- Docs & samples: migration guide, compatibility matrix, short and long examples for sync and streaming flows, negative tests for schema mismatch.
- Telemetry & observability: feature flags, per-route error/latency/quality histograms, regression alerts linked to prompt-eval sets.

Staged experiment plan:
1) Internal dogfooding (3 days): internal accounts only, feature-flagged in hosted API and in Dedicated staging pools. Acceptance: no P95 latency regression >10%, error rate <0.5% vs baseline, no structured-output regressions on our eval prompts.
2) Limited partner canary (7 days): 5-10 trusted customers opt into experiment via console toggle. Monitor quality metrics + open feedback channel. Acceptance: no high-severity customer bugs, documentation clarity verified by partners.
3) Gradual ramp (2 weeks): 10% -> 30% -> 60% rollout across new signups and opt-in existing customers. Each step gated by automated checks.
4) GA enablement: full release with deprecation timeline for legacy response shapes and SDK shims documented.

Rollback & remediation guidance (quick triggers):
- Automatic rollback if per-route token-error-rate doubles OR per-request latency P95 increases by >25% for 30m sustained.
- Manual rollback if qualitative evaluation shows structured-output hallucinations affecting >5% of prompts in baseline eval set.
- If errors caused by client SDK parsing: issue immediate compatibility patch and publish emergency patch notes.

Owners & signoffs:
- PM: Aisha Patel (launch owner)
- Eng owners: Ravi Kumar (runtime), Priya Shah (SDKs), Elena Gomez (telemetry)
- Docs/DevX: Luis Navarro (samples & migration guide)
- QA: Tiered test ownership by platform (integration, performance, chaos)

Acceptance criteria (per stage):
- Metrics: latency, token cost delta, error rate, structured-output precision/recall on labeled eval set.
- Docs: migration guide published, sample apps for streaming and function-calling in each SDK repo, automated snippets in docs site.
- Tests: end-to-end contract tests, schema fuzzer runs, CI gating on SDK release branch.

Trade-offs & notes:
- We will ship an SDK compatibility shim to avoid breaking existing customers immediately; this adds short-term maintenance burden but reduces churn risk.
- Strict rollout reduces blast radius but increases rollout time; chosen approach favors reliability over marketing speed.
- Structured-output verification requires labeled prompts; we use a mixed automatic + manual evaluation cadence for faster feedback.

Follow-ups:
- Schedule a 30-minute cross-functional dry run for the rollback playbook (owners listed above).
- Add canary customers to the console toggle list and communicate expected telemetry.
- Finalize PR checklist for SDK releases to include sample updates and API compatibility notes.
